source: KB differential reasoning for polymyositis vs dermatomyositis
distinguishing_text: Cross-reference this knowledge base's dermatomyositis entry. Distinguished from PM by (1) presence of characteristic skin findings (heliotrope rash, Gottron papules) and (2) a complement/microangiopathy-mediated mechanism (capillary lysis, perifascicular atrophy) rather than PM's direct CD8+ T-cell/perforin attack on myofibers (Dalakas & Hohlfeld, PMID 14511932). In a real single-centre cohort, dermatomyositis had significantly lower CK than PM (316 vs 4884 U/L, p=0.005) despite comparable clinical weakness, consistent with the differing injury mechanisms.

source: KB differential reasoning for dermatomyositis vs polymyositis
distinguishing_text: Polymyositis (PM) is mechanistically and clinically distinguished from DM by the ABSENCE of the characteristic cutaneous findings (no heliotrope rash, no Gottron's papules/sign) - PM is a 'diagnosis of exclusion' among the IIMs requiring that skin disease and other identifiable causes (drug-induced myopathy, muscular dystrophy, IBM) be ruled out. Pathologically, PM shows endomysial CD8+ T-cell infiltration of non-necrotic, MHC-class-I-expressing fibers rather than the perifascicular, complement/microangiopathy pattern of DM.

source: KB differential reasoning for acne_vulgaris vs rosacea
distinguishing_text: Rosacea is a key differential for facial acne-like eruptions in adults: it centres on the mid-face with persistent erythema, telangiectasia and inflammatory papules/pustules, but classically lacks comedones (a feature acne always has in some lesions), and it does not respond to standard acne therapy, requiring a distinct treatment strategy. Dermoscopically, features such as yellow/red halos, vascular polygons and follicular pustules have been shown to statistically differentiate rosacea from other facial inflammatory dermatoses.

source: KB differential reasoning for interstitial_cystitis vs urinary_tract_infection

Persistent symptoms despite negative repeated cultures and appropriate antibiotic trials point away from ongoing infection and toward IC/BPS.
